critical_issues.msg: run_gh uses text=True without an explicit encoding= — on Windows, locale.getpreferredencoding() returns cp1252, which corrupts non-ASCII characters (emoji, accented chars) in issue bodies
critical_issues.suggestion: Add encoding="utf-8", errors="replace" to the subprocess.run call, matching the fix already present in cleanup_orphan_subtasks.py

suggestions.msg: text=True is redundant when encoding= is also specified — in Python 3.7+ encoding= implies text=True
suggestions.suggestion: Remove text=True since encoding="utf-8" already implies it, or drop encoding= and keep text=True with a comment noting the Windows cp1252 risk

suggestions.msg: Return type annotation subprocess.CompletedProcess[str] is slightly imprecise — the generic should be CompletedProcess[bytes] for the base type, or not specified when using text mode
suggestions.suggestion: Use from __future__ import annotations or quote the annotation: 'subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]' as a string to avoid runtime resolution; or simply annotate as Any for simplicity

suggestions.msg: call_claude captures TimeoutExpired from subprocess but immediately returns a tuple instead of propagating the signal — callers have no way to distinguish a timeout from a runnable error, limiting their ability to retry or alert appropriately
suggestions.suggestion: Add --no-input to the gh/run_gh call to guarantee stdin is closed, and consider returning a distinct error string like 'timeout' alongside the None dict so callers can handle it differently if needed
